grade.first_issue: The negative-ratio homothety maps \(M_a\) to the point diametrically opposite \(D\), not to \(D\); hence the claimed collinearity \(S_{int},D,M_a\) is false.
grade.summary: Only preliminary homothety observations are valid. The proof then uses several false incidences and an unsupported final inference, so it does not establish that \(D'X\) passes through \(S_{int}\) or prove the required concurrency.
strengths: Correctly identifies tangent-direction correspondences under homothety and attempts to use the three-circles similitude theorem.

errors.description: \(S_{int}\) does not generally lie on \(AI\), so reflecting a line through \(S_{int}\) across \(AI\) does not preserve \(S_{int}\).
Since \(M_a\in AI\), its reflection across \(AI\) is itself, not the other arc midpoint as claimed.

The stated collinearities involving \(M_W\), \(M_a'\), and the similitude centers do not imply \(X,S_{int},D'\) are collinear; this unsupported inference is the entire concurrency argument. [Strict scoring rubric](/home/user/.codex/skills/strict-gold-informed-olympiad-scorer/SKILL.md)
